open.heading:
Four papers
{{nobody has to sit}}
body: None of the programmes below is compulsory, and none of them counts towards a board result. That is what makes entering them a decision — and the school names which ones it enters rather than describing a culture of enrichment in the abstract.

What each asks for is different in kind, which is the useful part for a family reading this: one is a written talent search, one is a defended project, one is an original idea, and one is a paper set from the primary years.
What has come back from them — the national qualifications and the placings — is recorded on {' '}Olympiad Achievements rather than repeated here.

list.heading:
A search, a defence,
{{an idea, a paper}}
body: Read side by side, the four programmes ask for four different things — and between them they cover most of what a science education is supposed to produce. A student who can sit a talent search may not be the one who can defend a project in front of a panel.
Where the work is actually done is on {' '}STEM, Robotics & Enrichment; CUET destinations are on {' '}University Counselling.
From time to time the school enables participation in other nationally notified science and academic programmes. It does not publish them as a standing list, so none is named here.

close.heading:
Named,
{{so it can be checked.}}
body: The school names the programmes it enters and the classes eligible for them. It does not publish a coaching timetable, how students are selected for entry, or whether preparation runs inside or outside the school day — and none of that is invented here.
